headline: Daily research brief — Thursday, October 8

items.title: TSLA's Oct 21 earnings is the only binary on the board; options price it above the median past reaction
items.detail: Options imply +/-7.9% via the Oct-23 ATM straddle vs a 5.95% mean-absolute reaction over the last four prints and a 3.51% median (the mean is skewed by July's -14.5% reaction, whose cause is unverified). The chain shows the classic event hump: 15-day IV 49.1% vs 8-day 38.9%. Selling premium into the Oct 23 expiry is short gamma into a scheduled binary - avoid.

items.title: The IV-vs-realized screen is compromised by the tape itself; no clean cheap or rich call
items.detail: QQQ, AAPL and MSFT are window-contingent - a single September day drives 32-40% of each 20-day realized window - with NVDA borderline. Implied vols of 11-36% (1-day ATM) look optically cheap against 45-130% trailing realized, but the desk issued no clean verdict: the spike days must roll off over the next 1-3 weeks first. No elevated-IV (premium-rich) signal anywhere today.

items.title: 10Y at 5.28%, up 56bp in two months; discount rates keep pressing growth multiples
items.detail: 2s10s at 51bp steepened 3bp on the day (10Y +1bp, 2Y -2bp); SOFR-EFFR flat at 0bp, no funding stress. The 2Y sits 89bp above the 3.88% fed funds rate - the front end prices easier policy ahead, which would reverse the headwind if it materializes. Until then, selling premium into NVDA/TSLA/MSFT means being paid for duration-driven multiple-compression risk.

items.title: Energy and grains stack catalysts into Friday
items.detail: EIA printed a fifth surprise crude draw (-3.186M bbl vs an expected build) and the curves stay backwardated; Tropical Storm Isaias threatens Gulf infrastructure with hurricane landfall expected late Friday - the freshest marginal catalyst on crude. The Oct WASDE lands tomorrow 12:00 ET with a corn yield cut as the tail risk against priced-in adequate supply (grains in contango). Black Sea vessel attacks are repricing war risk in European wheat basis, not yet in CBOT.

MSFT's raised $0.98 goes ex-div Nov 19.
